topic: Play Store launch: 5 things people forget

cover.headline: Before you hit Publish on Google Play, remember these 5 things
cover.subtitle: The small details that turn launch day into a week of waiting

slides.title: Your listing is your landing page
slides.description: Most people decide from the icon, the first screenshots and the short description.
bullets: Screenshots of real screens, not just slogans
Short description: 80 characters, make them count
slides.tip: Answer "what does it do?" in the first line of the full description.

rows.right: Targets the current required API level

slides.title: Version codes only go up
slides.description: Every upload needs a higher versionCode than the last one. Users see versionName; Play compares versionCode.
bullets: Bump versionCode for every build you upload
Pick a scheme you can keep, e.g. 10203 for 1.2.3
Automate the bump in CI so it never collides
slides.tip: Play rejects an upload that reuses a version code, so automate it before launch day.

slides.title: Roll out in stages
slides.description: You don't have to ship to everyone at once.
bullets: Start with a staged rollout to a small percentage
Watch crashes and ANRs in Android vitals
Halt the rollout if something breaks, then fix forward
slides.tip: Review times vary. Don't announce a launch date until the release is approved.

slides.title: Keep your keys safe
slides.description: Anything inside your app bundle can be extracted. Keep real secrets on your server, not in the APK.
bullets: Back up the upload keystore and its passwords
Never commit keystores or API keys to Git
Restrict API keys in each provider's console

slides.title: Launch day should be boring
slides.description: Do the checks before you upload, and launch day becomes the easy part.

caption.caption:
Most Play Store launch delays come down to small things that were easy to fix earlier.

This one covers your store listing, what a ready release looks like, version codes, staged rollouts and keeping your keys safe.

Play policies change often, so double-check the current requirements in Play Console.
caption.cta: Follow for more launch checklists, and save this one for your next release.
